newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn suggests compromise in NATO command row.
newsitem.headline: Bonn suggests compromise in NATO command row.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe on Sunday sought to break an impasse between Paris and Washington over who has control of NATO's Naples-based southern command by suggesting the post could be rotated.

Ruehe said a European and a U.S. officer could alternate in the job while the U.S. Sixth Fleet would be under the control of the Belgium-based Supreme Allied Commander of NATO forces in Europe, who is always a U.S. officer.
"This seems sensible and possible with the agreement of both sides," Ruehe told the Welt am Sonntag weekly newspaper.
France has insisted southern command must be headed by a European, reflecting the continent's desire to develop its own security identity within the alliance.
Paris has said it will consider stepping back from its commitment to rejoin NATO's military command if it is not satisfied with the alliance's Europeanisation.
The United States, however, has ruled out giving up southern command, which is currently responsible for the Sixth Fleet and is integral to Washington's Middle East policy.
The row has stalled efforts to streamline NATO's command structure following the end of the Cold War.
Military chiefs of staff ended a two-day meeting in Brussels on Friday unable to recommend a single reform plan to NATO ambassadors and having to present them with two options instead.
Some NATO sources have suggested the matter could only be sorted out at the highest political level and may have to wait for a summit of NATO leaders expected to be held next summer.
